[@Justin Murphy](/edgeware/account/kbeaMygw8HimVTB8WZxLUTEzygqS6ngrEqgmjAm6qNxbwUD) This is brilliant thanks for the feedback... we're learning as we go.

Some thoughts:

> If you want to continue with creator grants, perhaps you may consider offering a grants program with pre-defined grant amounts, and a standardized application, etc. This could maybe make things easier for you all, and the creators; and attract more creators by simplifying what they will be expected to deliver and what they can expect to receive.

Great point and definitely where we're headed. See this [previous post ](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1110-edgeware-grant-programme-structure-discussion)- a lot of this thinking will be present at the launch of [Kabocha](https://kabocha.network) since we are starting with a blank sheet of paper.

> In retrospect, I think splitting the grant into 3-4 milestones was somewhat counterproductive to the purpose of the grant—at least in my case. I completely understand the importance of de-risking by splitting it up, but in my case I think I failed to really access the “deep work” this grant was intended to buy me.

Also a valid point and perhaps the most important thing no-one discusses about this early stage of network grants / funding. Again we will be addressing in Kabocha... 

Truth is we need a better way to split the grant funding - aka the money that gives you the time do do the long deep work, and the ownership of the network, which is the speculative part of crypto ownership... the two do not play nicely together and offer competing motivations...

full_text:
[@Justin Murphy](/edgeware/account/kbeaMygw8HimVTB8WZxLUTEzygqS6ngrEqgmjAm6qNxbwUD) This is brilliant thanks for the feedback... we're learning as we go.

Some thoughts:

> If you want to continue with creator grants, perhaps you may consider offering a grants program with pre-defined grant amounts, and a standardized application, etc. This could maybe make things easier for you all, and the creators; and attract more creators by simplifying what they will be expected to deliver and what they can expect to receive.

Great point and definitely where we're headed. See this [previous post ](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1110-edgeware-grant-programme-structure-discussion)- a lot of this thinking will be present at the launch of [Kabocha](https://kabocha.network) since we are starting with a blank sheet of paper.

> In retrospect, I think splitting the grant into 3-4 milestones was somewhat counterproductive to the purpose of the grant—at least in my case. I completely understand the importance of de-risking by splitting it up, but in my case I think I failed to really access the “deep work” this grant was intended to buy me.

Also a valid point and perhaps the most important thing no-one discusses about this early stage of network grants / funding. Again we will be addressing in Kabocha... 

Truth is we need a better way to split the grant funding - aka the money that gives you the time do do the long deep work, and the ownership of the network, which is the speculative part of crypto ownership... the two do not play nicely together and offer competing motivations... 

> This is not unique to Edgeware, but personally I find the quantity and variety of communication channels and meetings to be completely overwhelming. 

True. It's basically a headfuck and again works against deep work and clear communication and instead rewards flitting between platforms, socials and results in fragmented thinking, comms and community... plus endless spats between people who are arguing over something with completely different information. 

Again, this simplification of comms is a core of Kabocha.  

> Between Telegram, Discord, Commonwealth.im, and the video calls—it would make my brain hurt to even start thinking “should I check in with the community this week?“ So I just found myself psychologically averse to everything altogether.

Amen. It's a tough balance, but its a great note and something we need to address since it's unsustainable and pointless to spend your entire week updating people on EVERYTHING that may or may not have happened.  

In general, the mantra of _underpromise and over-deliver_ plays well here... crypto is hype driven due to everyone building their 'Web3 companies' on 'Web2 incentives'. 

Web3 for me is the antithesis of Web2. It's about sustainable public funding, not monetising attention and therefore dragging us all out of anythign remotely like the present. We need to play a different game... that does mean a move away from the clicks / followers / vanity metrics and towards a more healthy, happy and sustainable way of communicating, creating and collaborating.

> Again not unique to Edgeware, but the price volatility was way harder to manage than I prepared for. I’m actually still hodling a lot of EDG; thankfully I was able to trade enough at opportune times that I I think I will still be in good shape after taxes, but this required a lot of active attention and I didn’t really appreciate the risk of a grant like this potentially even being a net-cost for me after taxes.

This is again a key priority to address with Kabocha and myself and [@Ramsey](/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) have been discussing this at length - the point I make above... _Truth is we need a better way to split the grant funding - aka the money that gives you the time do do the long deep work, and the ownership of the network._

Thanks again for this feedback - really really valuable,

body:
Hi Justin, seems like useful and fair feedback. 

Your proposal, as well as all of us that have made treasury proposals is part this experiment in how to fund different types of work, and we are all learning how to improve it. 

There seems to be a common thread across various funded proposals where they can feel sort of like an outsider that transacts with Edgeware. Especially people that may not be interacting in the Edgeware discord all the time, and thus feeling sort of detached from the "community". I would say though it is understandable, theres no need to feel that way!

I would say you and I and many funded proposals are actually very much what Edgeware is, and we are participating in the feedback process of testing and improving how these things are made. The funding may be partly expenditure but it's also a stake in the network, and a stake in the trajectory of this decentralised organisation. 

I agree in your point of overhwleming communication, but i wouldnt say it is a pre-requisite for teams.  I contribute full time in Edgeware building the Kabocha parachain, and I rarely participate in daily public communication. I may be on a group call once a week for Kabocha, and i talk to people directly or in very small group chats, as i feel its the best quality way to talk to people. I also make posts and updates on Medium and Subsocial. Long form talks are awesome and very effective like your podcast. People should be able to communicate in what works best for them. 

So all in all thanks for the update, and as closing opening question, how does all this  get better?

Missed your comment - for some reason it hadnt updated when I posted mine - maybe i needed to refresh browser. 

> People should be able to communicate in what works best for them. 

this...
Thanks for the detailed assessment of the process and value created Justin! Looking forward to the book.
